hints.title: Weighted Interval Scheduling Formulation
hints.text: Earning from a passenger ride equals end minus start plus tip. Rides cannot overlap in time.

hints.title: Group Rides by Destination Point
hints.text: Bucket rides according to their end point so that when computing maximum earnings up to point i, candidate rides ending at i are ready.

hints.title: Dynamic Programming Recurrence
hints.text: Define dp[i] as maximum earnings ending at or before point i: dp[i] = max(dp[i - 1], max over rides ending at i of dp[start] + earnings).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(n + M) where n is endpoint count and M is ride count
complexity.space: O(n + M) for dynamic programming table and ride adjacency buckets
complexity.notes: Linear scan over coordinate points avoids logarithmic binary search overhead.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all subset combinations leads to exponential complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping rides by destination avoids binary search per ride.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize weighted interval scheduling and solve with linear dynamic programming.
